title: The National Scala in Copenhagen
summary: They played the National Scala for dancing, an American novelty act, around New Year 1939 alongside Kai Ewans's big band.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: How long were you in Denmark, then?

Well, in Denmark we played there about... Oh, I don't know. Not quite a month. The picture that you see in the book Musicians Away From Home, that was at the National Scala, across from the Tivoli. At that time you had that band was playing... Kai(?) Owens. You remember Kai(?) Owens band? That was a big hit then. They had arrangements like Jimmy Lunceford?
Oh, in Denmark. Yeah, I remember them. How big a band did he have?
And you were still what? Six pieces?
Yeah. Well, nine pieces. Three. Bob (?), four. Four rhythm. About eight pieces. Kaiser Marshall...
And you were playing for dancing there?
Yeah, we played for dancing. We went into '39 New Year's. I remember playing New Year's there.
What sort of numbers did you play then?
Well, we were mostly an attraction(?) band.
You played Pops, though, were you?

Yeah. Attraction(?) (?)s, and jazz, old jazz. At that time, you see...American bands in those days... It was a novelty. They'd say, "American musicians from the Cotton Club and all that." You had (?)Wayne Wright(?), Little Lips... [LAUGHS]
Who did the singing in this group?
Everybody sang together, and Bobby... And his wife was a vocalist.
